questions.q: Ammonium cyanate (NH₄OCN) and urea ((NH₂)₂CO) are related as:
questions.explain: Both have the formula CH₄N₂O; ammonium cyanate is an ionic salt and urea a covalent molecule, so Wöhler's conversion is an isomerisation. Resonance structures would be the same compound, which these are not.

questions.q: In the usual classroom version of the Wöhler synthesis, which pair of aqueous solutions is mixed and heated to obtain urea?
questions.explain: Potassium cyanate and ammonium chloride exchange ions to give ammonium cyanate, which rearranges to urea on heating. NH₃ + CO₂ at high pressure is the modern industrial route, not the Wöhler synthesis.

questions.q: On heating, ammonium cyanate turns into urea through which pair of neutral species?
questions.explain: A proton passes from NH₄⁺ to OCN⁻, giving ammonia and cyanic acid, mostly as isocyanic acid HN=C=O. The lone pair of NH₃ then adds to the carbon of HN=C=O and a proton shift gives H₂N–CO–NH₂.

questions.q: Which reagent gives a quick test that urea has formed in the Wöhler synthesis, by forming a white precipitate?
questions.explain: Oxalic acid precipitates white urea oxalate from the solution. Silver and lead salts appear in Wöhler's own variants as cyanates, not as tests for urea.
